objective: Test the smallest natural per-component count refinement suggested by the complementary 4x5-k4 M2 and M3 failures: distinguish zero multiplicity, positive odd multiplicity, and positive even multiplicity while discarding exact positive magnitude.

candidate.name: ZOE
candidate.definition: For each exact canonical component type T, emit no symbol when n_T=0, O when n_T>0 is odd, and E when n_T>0 is even.
motivation: EW-RS-045 shows M2 erases scalar-load-bearing two-copy substitutions because n=2 collapses to zero.
EW-RS-046 shows M3 erases scalar-load-bearing three-copy substitutions because n=3 collapses to zero.
ZOE preserves whether a component type is present and the parity of its positive multiplicity while still identifying 1 with 3 and 2 with 4.

frozenKeys: PRESENCE = exact component type support only, ignoring multiplicity
ZOE = zero / positive-odd / positive-even per component type
ZOE_R3 = ZOE plus global rank modulo 3
antiCircularity: ZOE is defined before outcome qualification from the two already-frozen count-erasure mechanisms, not from individual W/D/L labels.
Every key depends only on current-rank exact component identities, multiplicities, and the explicitly declared rank grade.
Solved outcomes are used only to test class purity after key construction.
falsifiers: Any mixed scalar-value ZOE class rejects ungraded ZOE on 4x5-k4.
Any mixed ZOE_EXACT class proves that zero/odd/positive-even count information is insufficient even with exact rank.
M4, M6, and MULTI must reproduce their EW-RS-046 Q-V-exact controls or the harness is invalid.
nextIfZoePasses: Freeze ZOE as the leading count quotient and transfer it unchanged to the prior demanding carriers before re-deriving a compact scalar interaction law.
nextIfOnlyGradedZoePasses: Freeze the smallest passing rank grade with ZOE, then transfer that combined coordinate unchanged to prior demanding carriers.
nextIfZoeExactFails: Preserve the falsifier and test the next count-magnitude distinction; do not return to higher polynomial degree over parity.
